en: I worship Dattātreya, the god who wears matted locks, whose limbs are pale, who holds a trident in his hand, who is a treasure-house of compassion, and the remover of all diseases. || 1 ||
Of this mantra of the Śrī Dattātreya Stotra, the venerable Nārada is the seer (ṛṣi);
Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ); the Supreme Self, Śrī Datta, is the deity (devatā);
and its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of recitation for the pleasure of Śrī Datta.
Salutations to you, O Dattātreya, the creator of the origin of the world, the cause of its maintenance and dissolution, and the one liberated from the bonds of worldly existence. || 1 ||
O Dattātreya, naked embodiment of compassion, salutations to you who bring about the destruction of old age, birth, and death, and who purify the body. || 2 ||
Salutations to you, O Dattātreya, whose body possesses the splendor of camphor, who bears the form of Brahman, and who has mastered the Vedas and the Śāstras. || 3 ||
Obeisance to you, Dattātreya, who is devoid of shortness, length, thinness, and stoutness, as well as name and lineage, and who shines as one with the five elements. 4.
Salutations to you, O Dattātreya, the enjoyer of sacrifice, the purpose of sacrifice, the one who assumes the form of sacrifice, the lover of sacrifice, and the perfected one. || 5 ||
Brahmā in the beginning, Viṣṇu in the middle, and the god Sadāśiva at the end—
to you who are the very essence of these three forms, Dattātreya, obeisance be to you!

Obeisance to you, O Dattātreya, who dwell in the abode of enjoyment for the sake of worldly experience, who are fit for yoga, the sustainer, the conqueror of the senses, and the master of knowledge. 7.
O Digambara, O Divine One, who assumes a divine form, O Dattātreya, the eternally manifest Supreme Brahman—salutations be unto you! || 8 ||
O God Dattātreya, who dwells in the great field of Jambūdvīpa and in Mātāpura, victory to you; salutations be unto you. || 9 ||
Alms-gathering at every house in the village, a golden vessel in hand, and alms of manifold flavors—O Dattātreya, salutations be to you! 10.

O Dattātreya, you who possess the mudrā consisting of the knowledge of Brahman upon your garment and on the surface of the sky, for the sake of the awakening that is a mass of pure wisdom, salutations be unto you! 11.
Obeisance to you, O Dattātreya, whose nature is the supreme Brahman, the eternal bliss of the Avadhūta, and who possesses both a bodiless and an embodied form. 12.
O you whose form is truth, who are devoted to good conduct and the true Dharma, O Dattātreya, refuge of truth and beyond perception, salutations be unto you! 13.
O you who hold a trident in hand and a mace in your grasp, whose neck is graced with a forest garland;
O Brahman wearing the sacrificial thread, Dattātreya, salutations be unto you.
Obeisance to you, O Dattātreya, whose nature is both the perishable and the imperishable, who are higher than the highest, and to whom the supreme hymn of liberation has been offered. 15.
O Datta, Lord of Lakṣmī enriched with knowledge, grant [blessings] to me who am of the nature of your own self;
O Dattātreya, whose form is both possessed of attributes and devoid of attributes, salutations be unto you.
This hymn, which destroys enemies and bestows both knowledge and realization, causes all sins to be pacified; O Dattātreya, salutations be unto you! 17.
This great and divine hymn, which brings about direct perception [of the deity], was proclaimed by Nārada through the grace of Dattātreya. (18)
Thus ends the hymn to Dattātreya, composed by Nārada, in the glorious Nārada Purāṇa; it is perfectly complete.
